::: {.day-nav .kind-study}

:::

::: {.why}
An engine with a subtle bias will give a random strategy a nonzero expected return, and running 200 of them is the cheapest way to find out whether yours does.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the mean and distribution of Sharpe for random strategies through your engine, and state what it should be.
- Say what a nonzero mean would imply about the engine rather than about the strategies.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Analyse last night's 200 null runs: report the mean Sharpe with a standard error and test whether it differs from the small negative value that costs alone should produce. A mean above zero after costs means the engine has a bias, and the usual culprits are fill timing and the treatment of the first and last session.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Turn it into a permanent test: assert the mean null Sharpe lies within an interval around the cost-implied value, with enough replications that the test is powered to catch a bias of the size that would matter. Record the runtime, since a slow test is one you will disable.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Characterise the distribution too, since you will use it as the reference null for phase 6: report its standard deviation and the 95th percentile.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The null-strategy distribution is now a characterised property of the engine and a standing test. Phase 6 evaluates every signal against this distribution rather than against zero.
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A null-strategy test in the suite with the distribution characterised, and the mean tested against the cost-implied value.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your 200 null strategies have a mean Sharpe of plus 0.15 after costs. What is wrong, and where would you look first?
:::
